findings.description: AWS access key and secret access key are embedded in plaintext in the instance user_data script, which is stored in the EC2 metadata service and Terraform state, exposing long-lived credentials to anyone with instance or state access.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true, leaving data at rest unencrypted and readable if the underlying storage or snapshots are exposed.
The snapshot is taken from an unencrypted volume and does not enforce encryption, so the snapshot itself remains unencrypted and could be shared or accessed insecurely.
Ingress rule allows TCP port 22 (SSH) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing administrative access to the entire internet and enabling brute-force or credential-stuffing attacks.
Ingress rule allows TCP port 80 from 0.0.0.0/0 with no compensating controls (e.g., WAF, load balancer), directly exposing the web application server to the public internet.
Egress rule allows all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, which is overly permissive and increases the risk of data exfiltration if the instance is compromised.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, automatically assigning public IPs to instances launched in this subnet, increasing exposure to untrusted networks.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, automatically assigning public IPs to instances launched in this subnet, increasing exposure to untrusted networks.

findings.issue_category: missing encryption and public access controls
findings.description: The S3 bucket used for VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration and no public access block or bucket policy restricting access, risking exposure or tampering of sensitive network log data.
